LUMP/SWELLING IN NECK, AXILLA OR GROIN

How to aspirate lymph node for TB testing: • Clean skin over largest node with alcohol or povidone iodine. • Hold node in fixed position with one hand so that it will not move. Insert 18 gauge needle into node, draw back plunger 2-3mL to create vacuum. • Partially withdraw and reinsert needle at different angles several times (avoid withdrawing needle completely, maintain continuous vacuum). • Release vacuum pressure before withdrawing needle completely. • Remove syringe from needle, pull 2-3mL air into syringe, re-attach needle and gently spray contents of needle in a sputum bottle with saline. If pus, avoid adding saline. Request TB NAAT. • Ensure specimen type, site, HIV status and patient details are indicated on form.

• Review medication: atenolol, allopurinol, co-trimoxazole, phenytoin and antibiotics can cause a drug hypersensitivity reaction with lymphadenopathy. Discuss with doctor. • Is lymphadenopathy localised (neck or axilla or groin) or generalised (≥ 2 areas)?
Generalised
Neck Check scalp, face,
eyes, ears, nose, mouth and throat

• Manage as on symptom page. • Reassure patient lymphadenopathy should resolve with treatment. • If lymph node persists > 4 weeks, manage in adjacent column. Localised lymphadenopathy and well • Reassure patient. • Advise to return if symptoms develop. • If lymph node persists > 4 weeks, refer.
• Generalised lymphadenopathy or • Unwell or • Lymph node/s getting bigger quickly
Refer same week.

• Test for HIV 124, TB 102 and syphilis 66. Do full blood count. If abnormal, discuss with doctor. • If cough, weight loss, night sweats or fever: refer to doctor to aspirate lymph node for TB testing (see adjacent). If doctor not available/unable to aspirate or tests negative for TB, refer same week. • If contact with a probable/confirmed mpox case in the 21 days before symptom onset: with unexplained rash or lesion/s of skin/genitals/anus/rectum/mouth/eyes and ≥ 1 of: headache/backache/body pain, temperature > 38.5°C, fatigue, sore throat/nasal congestion/cough, consider mpox 40. • Check for symptoms/signs suggestive of cancer or if eligible for cancer screening 194. • If none of above, decide how to manage further:
Axilla • Check arms, breasts, chest, upper abdomen and back. • If lump in breast 55. No: check lower abdomen, legs, buttocks, genitals, anal region Yes: treat for bubo 65.
Groin Is the groin lymph node hot and tender?
Is medication or infective cause likely?
Localised: ask about other symptoms and look for cause (infection, rash, bite)
Approach to the patient with lump/swelling in neck, axilla or groin not needing urgent attention • If lump on the skin 89. If lump beneath skin, examine neck, inguinal area, axillae and perineum:
Thyroid mass likely if lump in neck that
moves up when patient swallows:
check TSH and refer same week.
Inguinal hernia likely if lump in groin
that gets bigger when standing/
coughing/passing stools: refer.

Hidradenitis suppurativa likely if recurrent, painful abscesses in axilla, groin or perineum • Discuss/refer all patients. Also check for diabetes 19, hypertension 148 and mental health 98. • If patient smokes, encourage to stop 164. If overweight/BMI ≥ 25 156.
• If none of above: a lump in neck, axilla or groin is likely an enlarged lymph node (lymphadenopathy). If unsure, discuss/refer.
